quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.
Speeding up quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: When you brake hard, you waste fuel getting back to speed. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Normally, vehicles at a four-way stop go in the order they arrive. When two arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires filled to the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tire tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water between the tire and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped ahead with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side and stop.
Keep driving at the same speed in your lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes if safe to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down at emergency scenes.

questions.question: You are driving uphill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass safely.
You may not be able to pass legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching from behind. On a hill with limited visibility, passing is illegal.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: There is an existing or possible hazard ahead.
There is a school zone ahead.
There is a public recreation area ahead.
There is food or gas ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is an existing or possible hazard ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or dangers ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you on the roadway. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and safely move to the right side of the road and stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: You see a green arrow on a traffic light. What can you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always let traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other drivers on the road.
Ignore what other drivers are doing.
Only drive on quiet side streets.
Avoid driving during busy times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other drivers on the road.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by using turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when needed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use a turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other vehicles moving into the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving to check road conditions.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal your left turn three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, and turn when the path is clear.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that you cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What maneuvers can you do from a center lane?

options.text: You can make left turns.
You can make U-turns.
You can pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can make left turns.
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: A blind spot is an area of the road that:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Is directly behind your vehicle.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery conditions. When road conditions are poor, safety may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and reverse to return to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your vehicle and others so you have time to react to mistakes made by other drivers.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in snow, rain, fog, or other dangerous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is coming. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a divider between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They're difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They're difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians even though they were looking. These are harder to spot because they are smaller and have less noticeable lights. Always watch carefully for them on the road.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: When is the road most dangerous?

options.text: After it rains.
After it has been raining for a couple of hours.
When it begins to rain.
Before it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it begins to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil and dirt on the road surface, creating a slick coating.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be prepared for?

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Be ready to steer to stay in your lane when passing large vehicles.
